gloss: to take someone out; to bring someone along

definitions.gloss: to take someone out; to lead someone outside; to bring someone along
definitions.explanation: To take a person (or sometimes a pet) from one place to another, typically from indoors to outdoors or from home to somewhere else.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}を{公園|こうえん}に{連|つ}れ{出|だ}す。
examples.english: To take the kids to the park.

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}を{散歩|さんぽ}に{連|つ}れ{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I took the dog out for a walk.

examples.japanese: {天気|てんき}がいいから、{家|いえ}にこもっている{弟|おとうと}を{無理|むり}やり{外|そと}に{連|つ}れ{出|だ}した。
examples.english: Since the weather was nice, I dragged my brother, who was cooped up at home, outside.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound verb formed from {連|つ}れる (to take along) and {出|だ}す (to take out). Emphasizes the action of bringing someone from one location (typically indoors) to another (typically outdoors).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {外|そと}に{連|つ}れ{出|だ}す (to take outside)
- {散歩|さんぽ}に{連|つ}れ{出|だ}す (to take out for a walk)
- {子供|こども}を{連|つ}れ{出|だ}す (to take the children out)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {連|つ}れて{行|い}く: to take along — more general, no emphasis on going outside
- {引|ひ}っ{張|ぱ}り{出|だ}す: to drag out — stronger nuance of forcing someone out
